divergences: `containerRef`, `fromRef` and `toRef` are typed `HTMLElement | null` rather than a required `HTMLElement`: a Vue template ref is `null` until the parent has mounted, so the idiomatic `:container-ref="container"` binding passes `null` on the first render. They are still required props (pass `null`, not nothing).
active testimonial index clamped when the list shrinks; empty list during transition resets to 0 instead of NaN (upstream fix, Svelte parity pending)
tooltip ids are generated per avatar with useFancyId, so aria-describedby stays a single token and unique across rows that share item ids (upstream fix, Svelte parity pending)

`AppleCardData.content` is a Vue component or render function (`Component` from `vue`), rendered through `<component :is="card.content">`, where the Svelte package takes a `Snippet`. It cannot become a slot: `content` lives inside an item of the `cards` array, not in a prop position, so there is no 1:1 snippet-to-slot mapping. Consumers pass `content: () => h('div', …)` or a small component instead of `{#snippet}`.

active option follows the highlighted suggestion by its text when the filtered list changes while open and clears when that suggestion is gone, so aria-activedescendant never points at a missing option (upstream fix, Svelte parity pending)

lowercase callbacks onpercentagechange, ondragstart, ondragend, onhoverenter, onhoverleave stay declared props, passed as :ondragstart etc; @dragstart / @hoverenter spellings compile to onDragstart / onHoverenter, are dropped and never fire

autoplay keeps a single frame loop: startAutoplay stops the running loop first so mount, hover leave, drag end and prop restarts no longer stack loops, and unmount cancels it (upstream fix, Svelte parity pending)

ComposerCommandMenu attaches its textarea `keydown` listener in the CAPTURE phase. The Svelte source gets handler ordering for free (its input part's keydown is a delegated root listener); in Vue every listener sits on the textarea itself and the input part's is registered first, so a bubble-phase `stopPropagation()` would arrive too late to stop Enter-to-send. Not visible in the component's API, but visible to a consumer who puts their own keydown listener on the textarea: the menu now runs ahead of it while open.

`Confetti`'s `fire()` reads the `options` prop at call time, but Vue hands a REASSIGNED `options` object to the child only on the parent's next render: a handler that does `options = { … }` and calls `fire()` in the same tick bursts with the PREVIOUS object, where the Svelte component bursts with the new one. Mutating the object already passed as `options` behaves identically on both sides, and the reassignment is deferred rather than lost — the next `fire()` after the parent re-renders uses it. Framework-inherent (Vue exposes no synchronous prop flush); pinned by ConfettiFire.test.ts:77-92.

ConfettiButton renders type="button": the Svelte source's bare <button> defaults to submit inside a form and inheritAttrs false leaves consumers no way to override it (upstream fix, Svelte parity pending)

Deliberate divergence, verified correct: `openAt` drops the source's imperative `anchorRef.style.setProperty("left"/"top")` writes, relying on the span's `:style` binding landing in the component-update pass ahead of the `flush: "post"` recompute. Proven end to end by the 'second right-click moves the panel' case (10/12px then 300/302px). Residue: a consumer reading `ctx.anchorRef.style.left` synchronously from inside `onOpenChange` sees the PREVIOUS coordinates in Vue and the new ones in Svelte.
onCopy reports the value captured when the copy started, not the prop's later value, when the prop changes while the clipboard write is pending (upstream fix, Svelte parity pending)

Scoped-CSS mapping: the child subject `:global(...)` becomes `:slotted(...)`, and the `:global()` wrappers inside `:has()`/`:not()` arguments are dropped (Vue never scopes pseudo-class arguments, and `:slotted()` there would emit invalid CSS). Net effect: Svelte scopes the root compound, Vue scopes the child compound — only direct children that arrived through the default slot dim. DOM injected into the root from outside the slot would not participate (Svelte's rule would still catch it).

The two `<style>` rules keep their declarations verbatim but lose their document-wide reach. The source wraps both in `:global()`, which — because this package aggregates scoped styles into one `dist/styles.css` every consumer imports once — would force a `.group\/card` 44px min-box and a `*{transition-duration:0.1s!important}` reduced-motion override on every app importing the package, including apps that never render this component. Here they compile to `.group\/card[data-v-…]` and `[data-v-…],[data-v-…-s]`: this component's own elements plus its whole slot subtree. Matches the React package's identical narrowing.
Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the 0.1s transition override therefore applies to this component and its slot content only, not to the rest of the host page.

pointer tracked in viewport client coordinates, not page coordinates, so the magnification lines up with the icons measured by getBoundingClientRect on a scrolled page; matches the React port (upstream fix, Svelte parity pending)
toggling manualMode after mount starts or stops the auto-cycle; switching to manual returns focus to the first word (upstream fix, Svelte parity pending)
a source url or href with no scheme gets https:// added before the scheme check, the same as SourceCard, so the marker no longer resolves against the app origin (upstream fix, Svelte parity pending)

`autocomplete` is widened to `string` in the props the component accepts; the exported `InputProps` still types it as the full autofill token union. The generated props type otherwise exceeds the type checker's union ceiling (TS2590), so a token typo is no longer caught at the call site.

`aria-label` is spelled `ariaLabel` in `LineHoverLinkProps`. Vue camelises declared prop names, so Svelte's hyphenated key can never be read back off `props` (it silently rendered nothing). Both `ariaLabel="…"` and the template spelling `aria-label="…"` reach the prop and emit `aria-label` on the anchor, matching Svelte's output.

Line height survives a font-only change. Svelte's `style:font` / `style:line-height` directives re-apply only the declaration whose value changed, so switching to a different weight/family at the same px size re-applies the `font` shorthand (which resets `line-height`) without re-applying the longhand, and the lines drift inside their fixed-height masks. Vue's style patch re-applies every key of the style object on each patch, in declaration order (`font` then `line-height`), so the Svelte bug does not reproduce. Behavioural parity with the React port, reached without its folded `32px/38px` shorthand: the emitted style attribute still reads `font: …; line-height: …`, like Svelte's.

`NavigationMenuContext` gains one readonly member the source has no counterpart for: `pendingFocusValue`. A Vue watcher's callback body is untracked, so the panel cannot subscribe to the pending request merely by CALLING `consumeFocusRequest()`; it names the value as an explicit watch source. Without it, pressing Enter on a trigger whose panel is already open (hover-opened) would never move focus into the panel. `consumeFocusRequest` is still the only way to take a request.
step precision counts the exponent of steps written in exponential notation (1e-7), so tiny fractional steps no longer round back to an integer (upstream fix, Svelte parity pending)

Cross-fade exit easing differs from the source, package-wide and shared with the React port: the source's bidirectional `transition:iconFade` reports direction "both" to preset(), so BOTH legs resolve to JS_EASINGS.out; usePresence's core passes a real "in"/"out" per leg (presence-core.ts:173-176), so the EXIT leg resolves to JS_EASINGS.in. Left unpinned because the React port leaves it unpinned too and React is the parity reference; pinning would make this the only component in either port overriding the foundation's deliberate per-leg direction.

PressableProps declares only scale/haptic/disabled/class — no `Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>, …>` of the seven owned listeners, per the package's own-props-only contract. Consequence: TypeScript no longer blocks a consumer from passing `onpointerdown`/`onpointerup`/`onpointercancel`/`onpointerleave`/`onfocusout`/`onkeydown`/`onkeyup` through `$attrs`, and Vue MERGES same-named listeners into an array instead of letting the later one win, so such a handler now fires alongside the wrapper's own (caller's first, since `v-bind="attrs"` sits where Svelte spreads `{...restProps}`) rather than being silently overridden. README: keep the "put your own handlers for those on the child instead" guidance and note it is advisory here, not type-enforced.

lowercase callbacks onfadein / onfadeout stay declared props, passed as :onfadein / :onfadeout; a @fadein / @fadeout listener compiles to onFadein / onFadeout and never fires; the computed --pb-* custom properties win over a consumer style

The generated `name` follows Vue's own `useId()` sequence and reads `v-0-name`, `v-1-name`, … instead of the Svelte id shape. It is SSR-stable and present on the very first server-rendered paint, as the Svelte source requires. NEW CAVEAT: Vue's `useId()` counter is per APP, not per page — two RadioGroups mounted in two SEPARATE Vue apps on one page both generate `v-0-name` and WILL fight over each other's selection. Inside one app they are distinct. Consumers mounting several apps must set `app.config.idPrefix` per app, or pass an explicit `name`. The Svelte and React packages have no equivalent hazard.

a disabled href anchor calls preventDefault on click so it no longer navigates; the Svelte source only returns early and aria-disabled / tabindex -1 do not stop a pointer click from following the href (upstream fix, Svelte parity pending)

Changing `once`, `threshold` or `rootMargin` no longer tears down and rebuilds the observer: `useInView` routes them through the core's `update()` (and keeps a spent `once: true` observer from re-firing). Same behaviour the React port already has.

a disabled Select rejects every commit and closes its panel if disabled while open, so a portalled row click can no longer change the value or fire onValueChange on a disabled control (upstream fix, Svelte parity pending)

The stream is keyed on the CONTENT of `lines`, never on the array's identity. An inline `:lines="['a', 'b']"` hands the component a freshly allocated array on every parent re-render; keying on identity would clear the pending timeouts, wipe the typed-out text and restart the whole animation each time. The source restarts only when a tracked value really changes, and an inline array literal in a Svelte template is not one. The array is serialised rather than joined, so `['ab']` and `['a', 'b']` — which stream differently — never collide on the same key. An in-place mutation of a reactive `lines` array still restarts the stream, matching the source's tracked index reads. The one remaining gap: a re-allocated array with equal content keeps the current stream running, where the Svelte side would restart it. Same trade-off as the React port.
a words change re-arms the reveal on the new spans and clears the previous run's timers instead of leaving replacement words invisible (upstream fix, Svelte parity pending)

`autocomplete` as the component *accepts* it is widened to `string`; the exported `TextareaProps` still types it as the full autofill token union. The props type the macro generates multiplies every prop's union together and the token set tips that product past the type checker's union ceiling once the component's boolean props are in it (`Input` hits the same ceiling). The widening is a superset — every token the source accepts still type-checks — but a typo in a token is no longer caught at the call site.

— same slot if it survived, else the closest one at or after it, else the last, else nothing highlighted. The Svelte component leaves the raw index in place, which can point past the end of a shorter grid or at a different time than the one arrowed to. Matches the React package, which closed the same gap.

the entrance and exit move from `<Toast>` to `<Toaster>`. A `<Toast>` rendered directly by a consumer no longer animates itself in or out (it paints at rest); through `<Toaster>` the motion is unchanged — same preset, 300ms/8px arrival, 200ms/4px departure, same reduced-motion collapse. Parity with the React port: a toast has no `open` boolean, so the per-item mount clock has to live with whatever renders the keyed list.

The auto-open for a failure is keyed on the `call.status` VALUE (`onMounted` + `watch(() => call.status, …, { flush: 'post' })`), not on the `call` object identity. Handing the card a fresh `call` object whose status is still `"error"` does not re-fire the auto-open, where Svelte's prop-identity tracking would re-run its `$effect`. Same behaviour as the React port. Observable only when a consumer drives `open` from outside AND re-creates the `call` object.

the tooltip appends its id to the trigger's existing aria-describedby list and removes only that id on close instead of overwriting and deleting the attribute; it also rewires listeners and aria-describedby onto a replacement trigger when the slot swaps its first element (upstream fixes, Svelte parity pending)

each instance uses its own generated gradient id with useFancyId for the gradient and its stroke reference, so two beams on one page no longer share one spring-animated gradient (upstream fix, Svelte parity pending)
